text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no signs or symptoms at all, which is why it is called the "silent killer".
snippet_highlighted_words: no signs or symptoms at all

list.snippet: Most people feel completely normal even when their numbers are very high.
Headaches, nosebleeds, or facial flushing do not reliably mean your blood pressure is high, except during a severe spike.

text_blocks.snippet: When blood pressure rises to dangerous levels (usually above 180/120 mm Hg), it can cause critical damage. Call 911 immediately if you have extremely high readings along with any of these warning signs:

list.snippet: Numbness or weakness on one side of the body
The only way to find out if you have high blood pressure is to measure it using a cuff.
You can get checked at an annual doctor visit, at a local pharmacy, or with a home monitor.
Learn more about guidelines and risks from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or the American Heart Association.
